earned_by: A published reproduction procedure (arXiv 2609.23015v1, Appendix B.2) for a claim that the author says rests on its Lean formalization.
question: Does the pinned formalization of Braun's bit-PHP lower bound build, report only standard axioms for every declaration its aggregate module lists, and pass a fresh kernel replay?

public_inputs.checkout_location: /home/jscul/external-audits/bit-php-check (outside this repository; third-party code built at the owner's request)

forbidden_inputs: edits to the pinned sources, toolchain or dependency pins
primary_observable: exit status of each command; the axiom set reported for each of the seven declarations listed by claims/BitPHPPreprintRevision1.lean; the elaborated type of MathResearch.bitPHP_exponential
controls: A copy of the aggregate's audit with an extra declaration whose proof is sorry must be reported with sorryAx (the axiom check can fail).
A copy of the main theorem with the constant 32768 replaced by 1 must be rejected by Lean (the bound is not vacuous for the proof as written).
decision_rule: Pass: all three commands exit 0, every listed declaration depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and both controls fail as intended. Any other outcome is recorded exactly; nothing is patched.
stop_rule: Stop at the first failing command and record its output; otherwise stop after the controls.
nonclaims: A clean replay shows only that the formal statements follow from the formal definitions in Lean's kernel with Mathlib; whether those definitions are the standard ones is ticket B.
No assessment of the paper's prose, literature claims or novelty.
